title: Comparatives 8: Saying "Less" with менее
description: Менее ('less') sits before an ordinary adjective to make a comparative in the opposite direction. The adjective agrees with its noun; менее never changes. Some adjectives, like -ский words, only build the comparative this way.
descriptionRussian: «Менее» ставится перед обычным прилагательным и образует сравнительную степень в обратную сторону. Прилагательное согласуется с существительным; «менее» не меняется. Некоторые прилагательные (например, на -ский) образуют сравнительную степень только так.
intro: The same two-word construction pointed the other way. Russian has no one-word form meaning 'less X' for an arbitrary adjective, so this is the only route to that meaning, wherever the phrase sits. One group of adjectives has no one-word comparative at all, so those always take a two-word form in either direction.
rules: Put менее ('less') before a normal adjective to make a comparative in the opposite direction: менее интересный, менее важный.
The adjective after менее agrees with its noun in gender, number, and case; менее itself never changes.
Before a noun you must use the two-word менее form, because a one-word comparative cannot sit there: менее интересная книга.
Adjectives ending in -ский (русский, английский, немецкий) have no one-word comparative, so they always use более or менее.
examples: Это менее интересный фильм. (This is a less interesting film.) менее + masculine интересный, before the noun.
Эта книга менее интересная, чем та. (This book is less interesting than that one.) менее after the subject; the adjective is feminine to match книга.
Антон купил менее дорогой телефон. (Anton bought a less expensive phone.) менее + masculine дорогой, before the noun.
Это менее важное письмо. (This is a less important letter.) менее + neuter важное, agreeing with письмо.
Этот учебник менее русский по стилю. (This textbook is less Russian in style.) русский has no one-word comparative, so менее is the only option.
В магазине есть менее дорогие телефоны. (The shop has less expensive phones.) менее + plural дорогие, agreeing with телефоны.

items.promptEnglish: This is a less interesting film than that one.
items.hint: The English says 'less.' Which word means 'less'?
items.explanation: Менее means 'less,' so менее интересный matches 'less interesting.' The masculine ending -ый agrees with фильм.

items.promptEnglish: Masha bought a less expensive dress.
items.hint: Платье is neuter, and the form sits before the noun.
items.explanation: Before the noun you need the two-word form, and the adjective agrees with neuter платье: менее дорогое.

items.promptEnglish: This article is less important than that one.
items.hint: Which option means 'less' and matches feminine статья?
items.explanation: Менее важная means 'less important' and the feminine ending -ая agrees with статья.

items.promptEnglish: This is a less interesting book than that one.
items.hint: Before the noun книга. Which form can agree and means 'less'?
items.explanation: Before a noun you must use the two-word form, and менее интересная agrees with feminine книга.

items.promptEnglish: The shop has less expensive phones.
items.hint: Plural noun телефоны, and the form sits before it.
items.explanation: Before the plural noun телефоны you need the two-word form agreeing in plural: менее дорогие.

blanks: Антон выбрал _____ путь до работы. (Anton chose a less convenient route to work.)
Эта работа _____ , чем та. (This job is less interesting than that one.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: First blank: before the masculine noun путь you need the two-word form, agreeing in masculine: менее удобный. Second blank: работа is feminine, so менее интересная agrees.

errorCorrection.sentence: Это менее интересный книга, чем та.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This is a less interesting book than that one.
errorCorrection.explanation: The adjective after менее agrees with its noun. Книга is feminine, so the masculine интересный must become feminine: менее интересная книга.

errorCorrection.sentence: Маша ищет дешевле машину для города.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha is looking for a less expensive car for the city.
errorCorrection.explanation: A one-word comparative like дешевле cannot stand before a noun, so you switch to the two-word менее form and make it agree. Машину is the feminine object, so the adjective is feminine дорогую: менее дорогую машину.

errorCorrection.sentence: Этот учебник менее руснее по стилю.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This textbook is less Russian in style.
errorCorrection.explanation: Русский is a -ский adjective with no one-word comparative, so руснее is not a real word. You build the comparative with менее plus the plain adjective: менее русский.

errorCorrection.sentence: Антон купил более дорогой телефон, но хотел менее.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton bought a less expensive phone.
errorCorrection.error: более дорогой телефон, но хотел менее
errorCorrection.explanation: The English says 'less expensive,' so use менее, not более: менее дорогой телефон. Более means 'more,' the wrong direction.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: This is a less interesting article.
minimalPairs.explanation: Before a noun you need the two-word form, and менее интересная agrees with feminine статья. The one-word интереснее cannot sit before a noun.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: This film is less interesting than that one.
minimalPairs.explanation: The adjective after менее agrees with its noun. Фильм is masculine, so менее интересный is correct. Менее интересная is feminine and does not match фильм.

sentenceBuilding.translation: This is a less interesting book.
sentenceBuilding.hint: менее stays put; the adjective is feminine to match книга, and it sits before the noun.

sentenceBuilding.translation: Anton bought a less expensive phone.
sentenceBuilding.hint: Subject, then verb, then менее + masculine adjective before the noun телефон.

sentenceBuilding.translation: This is a less important letter.
sentenceBuilding.hint: письмо is neuter, so the adjective takes the neuter ending -ое.

reviewVocab.definition: -ский adjectives have no one-word comparative, so they always take более or менее: менее русский, менее английский
